lesson.title: What are we doing tomorrow?
lesson.scenario: Knafeh and Fattoush want to visit Knafeh’s family after work. They move from an idea to an agreed time.

steps.instruction: Ask about tomorrow’s shared plan, not yesterday’s actions.

answers.meaning: What did you do today? (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This asks Knafeh what he already did today.

answers.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This checks in with Knafeh instead of asking about tomorrow’s shared plan.

answers.meaning: What will we do tomorrow?
answers.rationale: Raḥ plus the “we” form and bukra asks about a shared future plan.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Raḥ plus the “we” form and bukra asks about a shared future plan.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Knafeh suggests visiting his own family after work. Speak as Knafeh.

answers.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?
answers.rationale: Ahli identifies Knafeh’s family when Knafeh speaks; after work supplies the ordering.

answers.meaning: Shall we visit your family after work? (to Fattoush)
answers.rationale: This would mean Fattoush’s family, changing whose family they visit.

answers.meaning: I worked, then visited my mother.
answers.rationale: This recounts completed work and a visit rather than making tomorrow’s suggestion.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ahli identifies Knafeh’s family when Knafeh speaks; after work supplies the ordering.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Knafeh is speaking, so use “my family.”

steps.instruction: You like the visit idea but still need the time. Ask for it.

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.meaning: How’s your family? (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This asks how the family is rather than when to visit.

answers.meaning: Okay. What time?
answers.rationale: Ayy sāʿa asks for a clock time after accepting the idea.

answers.meaning: Do you want tea or coffee? (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This offers drinks rather than settling the schedule.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ayy sāʿa asks for a clock time after accepting the idea.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Ask for the missing clock time.

steps.instruction: The agreed time is six. Give that time.

answers.meaning: At six o’clock.
answers.rationale: Sitte sets six o’clock, matching the agreed time.

answers.meaning: At seven o’clock.
answers.rationale: Sabʿa sets seven, an hour later.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow
answers.rationale: Tomorrow gives the day but not the clock time.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Sitte sets six o’clock, matching the agreed time.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Choose the time, not only the day.

steps.instruction: Fattoush confirms: tomorrow, six, Knafeh’s family. Preserve all three details.

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.arabic: تمام، اليوم الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, il-yōm is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, today at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: The family and time fit, but this changes tomorrow to today.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: The day and family fit, but this changes six to seven.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: The confirmation carries forward day, time, and whose family.

evaluation.correctExplanation: The confirmation carries forward day, time, and whose family.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Check each detail rather than matching only the family.

steps.instruction: In this plan, the visit follows work. Choose “after work.”

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.meaning: Before work
answers.rationale: This reverses the relationship to work.

answers.meaning: After work
answers.rationale: This places the visit after work finishes.

answers.meaning: At work
answers.rationale: This describes a location or work setting, not the requested sequence.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This places the visit after work finishes.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 1: a new plan uses seven instead of six. Give the new time.

answers.meaning: At seven o’clock.
answers.rationale: Use sabʿa to transfer the timing pattern to the revised plan.

answers.meaning: At six o’clock.
answers.rationale: This keeps the earlier time despite the change.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow
answers.rationale: This gives only the day.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Use sabʿa to transfer the timing pattern to the revised plan.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 2: confirm tomorrow at seven with Fattoush. Say that you will drink tea together.

prompt.meaning: Shall we drink tea together tomorrow?

answers.arabic: آه، اليوم الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, il-yōm is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, today at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This changes tomorrow to today.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This repeats the previous visit plan at six instead of the revised tea plan at seven.

answers.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This confirms the new day, time, and shared activity.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This confirms the new day, time, and shared activity.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Keep all three details of the new arrangement.

lesson.unitTitle: Everyday conversations with someone you love

introduction.goal: Suggest a shared visit, ask for a time, and confirm tomorrow’s plan.

line.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

line.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
line.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
line.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

expressions.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

expressions.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
expressions.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
expressions.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)

introduction.usageNote: A useful plan gives the day, the time, and the shared activity. Bukra supplies tomorrow; the reply need not repeat raḥ when the future setting is clear. These scenes share an evening context; clarify morning or evening in real arrangements.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target. Ahli is the speaker’s family. When Fattoush confirms Knafeh’s proposal, it becomes ahlak, his family as her listener. Niʿmal/nzūr/nishrab are shared actions in these phrases. Raḥ is a future marker here, distinct from past rāḥ, “he went.” Transliteration: ā/ī/ū and ē/ō mark long vowels; ʿ = ع, ḥ = ح, ʾ = glottal stop, sh = ش, kh = خ, gh = غ. Doubled letters are held longer. Jordanian alternatives are not introduced in this unit.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings yet. This six-turn transcript is the recording script: Fattoush uses feminine self-description; Knafeh uses masculine self-description. Read each speaker’s turns in order, then the practice prompts and answer options as separate clips. Retain the marked address distinctions. A Palestinian speaker and owner must check wording/pronunciation before assets are labeled reviewed. Optional device speech is a variable browser preview, not a dialect model.

teachingCards.title: Open tomorrow’s shared plan
teachingCards.note: Raḥ points forward; niʿmal is we do or make. Bukra supplies tomorrow, so this is a shared future plan.
teachingCards.recallCue: Ask Fattoush what the two of you will do tomorrow.

teachingCards.title: Add who and when

phrase.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

teachingCards.note: Ahli names your own family. Baʿd ish-shughl puts the visit after work; baʿdēn by itself means then.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Suggest visiting your family after work.

teachingCards.title: Ask for the missing detail
teachingCards.note: Tamām accepts the idea. Ayy sāʿa asks for the time, completing the arrangement.
teachingCards.recallCue: Accept the visit idea, then ask what time.

teachingCards.title: Give the first time
teachingCards.note: Is-sāʿa introduces the clock time. The dialogue shares an evening context; in a real plan, clarify morning or evening if needed.
teachingCards.recallCue: Knafeh asks what time. Say six o’clock.

teachingCards.title: Change one piece of the plan
teachingCards.note: Keep the time frame and change just the number. Sabʿa is seven; sitte is six.
teachingCards.recallCue: In a new arrangement, the time is seven instead. Give the new time.

teachingCards.title: Confirm the whole new arrangement

phrase.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
phrase.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
phrase.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.

teachingCards.note: Combine the day, time, and activity. Sawa keeps the tea plan shared; the tomorrow context makes its future setting clear.
teachingCards.recallCue: Accept tomorrow at seven and confirm drinking tea together.
